chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Accurate T-staging is crucial for personalized treatment of laryngopharyngeal cancer... Pathology-based staging is invasive and time-consuming, while manual review of an entire 3D CT volume is labor-intensive and subjective... Existing computer-aided approaches have two major limitations. First, whole-volume models and isolated tumor masks underrepresent the anatomy-structured pattern of tumor spread... Second, conventional multimodal methods fuse global CT and report representations, making it difficult to align individual anatomical structures with their corresponding textual findings.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the clinical importance of T-staging, the limitations of manual CT review, and the structural and alignment challenges of existing computer-aided methods.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: We propose an annotation-free multimodal framework that combines CT-derived organ features with organ-specific evidence from radiology reports. The framework contains three components: Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG), Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA), and Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG).
chk_method.reason: The poster correctly identifies the proposed framework and its three key components (AOG, OCA, and REG).

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: We introduce an anatomy-structured multimodal framework that integrates 3D CT volumes and radiology reports for laryngopharyngeal cancer T-staging without manual tumor masks... Evaluation on 656 patients from four centers demonstrates consistent improvements over strong image-only and multimodal baselines in binary and three-class staging. The model generalizes to external cohorts, remains robust to segmentation noise and report variation, and performs on par with or better than experienced radiologists.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster's conclusion matches the paper's main conclusion that the proposed framework consistently outperforms baselines and performs on par with or better than experienced radiologists.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Error analysis identifies two dominant patterns. Nine of sixteen errors are over-staging cases, often caused by reports describing cartilage invasion that pathology does not confirm. Seven are under-staging cases, frequently associated with reports that omit invasion or state that invasion is absent despite pathological confirmation. These findings reflect inherent CT-pathology discordance rather than simple cross-modal misalignment and motivate uncertainty-aware fusion and clinical review of borderline cases.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster accurately describes the limitation regarding inherent CT-pathology discordance leading to over-staging and under-staging relative to pathological ground truth.
